body.statement: Let \(R\) be a real closed field, let \(L\subseteq R[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\) be an ideal, and let \(f\in R[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\).  The polynomial \(f\) vanishes at every point of the real variety of \(L\) if and only if there are an integer \(a\geq1\) and finitely many \(q_i\in R[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\) such that \(f^{2a}+\sum_iq_i^2\in L\).

attestation.note: The displayed statement is the equality-only specialization of the cited Real Nullstellensatz; the stable DOI is supplied because no source transcription is embedded.
